body:
## Maintainer ruling recorded

Ruled 2026-08-24, live PM chat, verbatim: 「其他按照你的建议继续」 (adopting the skills seat's four-facet digest, which recommended A with the no-forced-flip stock treatment).

**Ruled: A — the audience-posture vocabulary**, with the stock sub-decision settled as recommended:

1. One declaration answers "who can become this app's user": closed vocabulary `invite_only | email_domain | open`, one enforcement point, out-of-vocabulary values refused loudly (the `membershipPolicy` shape).
2. Invariant: any posture other than `invite_only` forces email verification.
3. The permission set a self-registrant receives must be explicitly declared — the implicit fallback retires.
4. **New environments default `invite_only`; existing environments keep current behavior** + a prominent console notice + one-click switch. ⛔ No forced-flip date — silently breaking live user registration on deployed stacks is rejected.
5. ⛔ Not in scope (recorded so it stays out): token join links, approval queues, per-app posture, per-link roles, SCIM interplay, custom onboarding flows. The frozen cloud-org join-link epic #11586 stays frozen; a future `link` posture may reuse its token shape.

Implementation is Clause-② (spec AuthConfig surface + enforcement + publish-time completeness predicate per the ADR-0078 family) — contract-review tier on the PR; spec/services surfaces to be split by the owning seats at claim time. `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Progress — sub-issue A is MERGED.**

- [x] **A — objectstack#11739** → PR #11767 merged as `4f24e9d2e` on framework `main` (2026-08-25). Two review rounds and two contract reviews (round 2 covered the landing-window sync + the bootstrap-bypass fix). All 38 checks green at the merged head.
- [ ] **B — cloud#1649** → unblocked and returned to `pm:queue` today, with a scope correction recorded on that card.

**What actually shipped, against what this epic ruled:** the closed vocabulary `invite_only | email_domain | open` with `invite_only` as the undeclared default, one decision owner on the creation path, forced email verification for every self-registration-permitting posture, a declared self-registrant permission set that is actually granted, and the ADR-0087 semantic migration `audience-posture-default-invite-only` registered for the secure-default flip. Shipped `minor` per the launch-window rule, as ruled.

**Two things learned in flight that the epic did not anticipate**, both now closed in the merged work:

1. better-auth 1.7.1's sign-up route converts a 403 from the `validateUserInfo` admission seam into a synthetic **200** whenever `requireEmailVerification` is on — and this epic's own invariant forces verification on for exactly the postures that gate self-registration. The wall would have been inert precisely where it matters, with nothing red. Caught by measurement, fixed by raising the same decision in the `/sign-up/email` before-hook.
2. The framework's pre-existing "a fresh install must never lock its operator out" bootstrap bypass **never fired on any real deployment**: its probe called `findOne` with no predicate, which the real ObjectQL engine refuses (#4419), and the surrounding `catch` read that refusal as "users exist". The audience gate inherited the same dead probe and turned it into red CI. Both now route through one answerable, fail-closed helper, and `isHumanUserRow` is the single owner of the population predicate.

Findings filed along the way: objectstack#11957 (engine doubles answer a predicate-less `findOne` the real engine refuses — why a 641-line green matrix was blind to #2), objectstack#11959 (a third hand-spelled copy of the human-user predicate in plugin-security), objectstack#11770 (the invitation carve-out stops admitting past 200 pending invitations).

**Adjacent P0 opened while verifying this epic's outcome locally**: objectstack-ai/cloud#1653 — a new user can sign up on production and then cannot create their workspace, because the control plane's degraded tenancy posture makes `organization/create` refuse. It is not part of this epic, but it gates whether any of this reaches a new customer at all.

**Epic complete — closing.** Both sub-issues landed and verified:

- [x] **A — objectstack#11739** (PR #11767, merged `4f24e9d2e`): the closed audience vocabulary `invite_only | email_domain | open`, default `invite_only` with no legacy limbo, one decision owner on the creation path (including the vendor sign-up shield raise the measurement forced), forced email verification for self-registration postures, the declared self-registrant permission set actually granted, ADR-0087 semantic migration registered, shipped `minor` per the launch-window rule. Along the way it exposed and fixed the never-fired bootstrap bypass (its probe called a predicate-less findOne the real engine refuses), and follow-ups hardened the invitation carve-out past its 200-row ceiling (#11770) and the walled owner's operator-provisioned verification (#12751, ruled 2026-08-28).
- [x] **B — cloud#1649** (PR #1714, merged `f3b78e2e2`): both real provisioning writers share one path and declare `invite_only` explicitly; the switch action rides the environment's declarative surface with the framework's own schema doing every refusal; the backfill ships as the auditability chore the scope correction sized it as; the assembled `audience` object reaches the tenant kernel verbatim and is OMITTED when undeclared, so the framework's default rules alone.

The business outcome the epic was opened for: an operator can flip an environment to `email_domain` with their company domains and post a registration link in any group chat — the gate is on the domain, not on link secrecy — or leave it `invite_only` (the fleet default) where nobody self-registers at all. One residual verification is scheduled, recorded on cloud#1649's ACCEPT: this seat reads a freshly provisioned staging env's `/api/v1/auth/config` after the next timer deploy to confirm `audiencePosture: 'invite_only'` lands on a real tenant kernel.
